facts.text: The fairy martin is a dumpy, square-tailed swallow that averages 12 centimetres long and weighs just 11 grams.
facts.quote: The fairy martin is dumpy and square tailed. It averages 12 centimetres (4.7 in) long and weighs 11 grams (0.39 oz).

facts.text: Adults have an iridescent blue back, brown wings and tail, a rufous crown and nape, and a whitish rump.
facts.quote: The adult has an iridescent blue back, brown wings and tail, a rufous crown and nape, and a whitish rump.

facts.text: You can pick a fairy martin out from other Australian swallows by its pale rump.
facts.quote: This species can be distinguished from other Australian swallows by its pale rump.

facts.text: The fairy martin's call is a chrrrr and its song is a high-pitched twitter, higher than the tree martin's.
facts.quote: The call of this vocal swallow is a chrrrr and the song is a high-pitched twitter. The vocalizations are higher pitched than those of the tree martin.

facts.text: Fairy martins breed from August to January, and the largest known colony contained 700 nests.
facts.quote: Fairy martins breed from August through to January in colonies usually of a few tens of nests, but the largest known site had 700 nests.

facts.text: The nest is a bottle-shaped structure of up to a thousand mud pellets, lined with dried grasses and feathers.
facts.quote: The nest is a retort- or bottle-shaped structure, made from up to a thousand mud pellets and lined with dried grasses and feathers.

facts.text: Both sexes build the nest and share incubation and care of the young.
facts.quote: Both sexes build the nest and share incubation and care of the young.

facts.text: A clutch is usually four reddish-brown speckled white eggs, and pairs often raise two or three broods a season.
facts.quote: The clutch is usually four, sometimes five, reddish-brown speckled white eggs, and this species is often double or triple brooded.

facts.text: Fairy martins feed high in the air on flying insects, but will also snatch injured moths from a newly cut lawn.
facts.quote: The fairy martin feeds high in the air on flying insects, usually in large flocks. Fairy martins have a slow fluttering flight and feed higher than welcome swallows. They will also feed on insect swarms low over water, and have been recorded feeding on injured moths on a newly cut lawn.

facts.text: After breeding, abandoned mud nests may become roosts for several species of microbats.
facts.quote: When the mud nest is vacated after breeding, it may become occupied by several species of microbats.
